newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Brown says no extra taxes in manifesto.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Brown says no extra taxes in manifesto.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party manifesto, to be published on Thursday, will contain no promises which would involve extra taxes, economic spokesman Gordon Brown said on Wednesday.
"There will be no public spending pledges, as you will see in the manifesto tomorrow, which require there to be extra taxes," Brown told a news conference ahead of the May 1 national election.
Brown attacked Prime Minister John Major for his pledge to introduce tax reforms to help families in the second year of a new Conservative government.
"The first tax change will be in the second year of a Consrvative government but he doesn't say where the money is coming from," Brown said.
He said Major was introducing a new element in the debate between the two parties, who had both previously said they would implement tax cuts only when the economy could afford them.
